knowledge_base: Reference pages exist to answer 'what does this do' fast; tutorials answer 'how do I get started'; do not mix the two.
Quick-start sections that fit on one screen convert browsers into users; longer quick-starts get scrolled past.
Every code example should be copy-paste runnable; if it depends on setup, that setup belongs above the example.
Linking to source code with stable permalinks (a tag or sha) keeps docs from rotting when files move.
Audience-shaped voice: 'you' for contributors and end users, 'we' for researchers when discussing design.
Docs that fail to mention failure modes are half-finished; list the most common error and how to recover.
Examples should cover: minimal happy path, realistic happy path, common error path; that is enough for a reference.
Avoid passive voice in API docs; 'the registry loads metadata' is clearer than 'metadata is loaded by the registry'.
Cross-link related modules with 'See also' so readers can navigate by concept, not just alphabetical sidebar.
Version the docs alongside the code; out-of-sync docs cost more credibility than missing docs.
